title: Stable Sigmoid
statement: Implement `sigmoid(z)` for a real logit z. Return 1 / (1 + e^(−z)). For z greater than or equal to 0 evaluate exp(−z). For negative z evaluate exp(z) / (1 + exp(z)) so the exponential never overflows.
constraints: Use the stable branch described in the statement

hints: Large positive logits approach 1 and large negative logits approach 0.

approaches.name: Branch on sign
approaches.explanation: The two algebraically equal forms keep the exp argument non-positive.

editorial: The logistic function σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) maps a logit to a probability. Its derivative is σ(z) (1 − σ(z)), which is why logistic regression and sigmoid output layers train with a simple gradient. A naive exp(−z) overflows when z is a large negative number. Branching so the exponent is always ≤ 0 keeps the value finite and matches the mathematical function.
